description: Full event or sensitive object serialised directly into log statement
impact: PII or account data can be retained in CloudWatch Logs and exported to downstream systems, creating GDPR and PCI-DSS exposure.
fix_summary: Redact or mask sensitive event fields before serialising anything to logger calls.

description: Possible hardcoded secret — sensitive variable name assigned a string literal
impact: Hardcoded credentials can leak through source control, deployment bundles, or logs and are difficult to rotate safely.
fix_summary: Load credentials from Secrets Manager or Parameter Store at startup instead of embedding literals.

description: eval() or exec() called — code injection risk if argument contains user input
impact: Attacker-controlled expressions can execute arbitrary Python in the Lambda runtime.
fix_summary: Replace eval/exec with safe parsing such as ast.literal_eval or explicit dispatch tables.

description: urllib.request.urlopen() or requests call without HTTPS scheme validation
impact: Unvalidated URLs can reach internal metadata or private services from within the Lambda VPC or AWS network plane.
fix_summary: Parse the URL and require an https scheme and non-empty host before opening it.

description: Insecure deserialization: pickle.load/loads or yaml.load() without safe Loader
impact: Pickle and unsafe YAML loaders can instantiate attacker-chosen objects and execute code paths during load.
fix_summary: Use safe formats such as JSON or yaml.safe_load, and never unpickle untrusted bytes.

description: Command injection risk: os.system/os.popen/subprocess with shell=True
impact: Shell metacharacters can turn an operational helper into arbitrary command execution inside the Lambda runtime.
fix_summary: Use subprocess with shell=False and explicit validated arguments.

description: Weak cryptographic algorithm: MD5 or SHA-1 used — not suitable for security purposes
impact: MD5 and SHA-1 are unsuitable for integrity or security checks and can be collided or brute-forced.
fix_summary: Use SHA-256 or stronger algorithms, and dedicated password hashing for secrets.

description: TLS certificate verification disabled: requests called with verify=False
impact: Disabling certificate validation allows man-in-the-middle interception or spoofing of upstream services.
fix_summary: Remove verify=False and use a trusted CA bundle for private PKI.

description: XML parsing without XXE protection — xml.etree.ElementTree is vulnerable to XXE attacks
impact: XML external entities can read local files or trigger SSRF-style network access during parsing.
fix_summary: Switch to defusedxml or explicitly disable dangerous XML features.

description: Possible SQL injection — string formatting used to build a SQL query
impact: Dynamic SQL construction lets attackers alter queries, exfiltrate data, or corrupt records.
fix_summary: Use database-driver parameter binding instead of string interpolation.

description: User-controlled value logged without sanitization — potential log injection
impact: Embedded control characters can forge log lines, break parsers, or hide malicious activity in CloudWatch.
fix_summary: Sanitize, quote, or truncate user-controlled log values before interpolation.

description: Silent exception swallowing: except block with only 'pass' — errors are hidden
impact: Important failures disappear, making abuse and operational defects impossible to detect or investigate.
fix_summary: At minimum, emit a debug log with stack information when intentionally suppressing an exception.

description: Sensitive key name in function return value — may expose secrets to caller
impact: Secrets or tokens may be returned to API callers, chained Lambdas, or audit logs.
fix_summary: Strip or mask sensitive keys before returning a response object.

description: Event parameter used in AWS API call without format validation
impact: Passing malformed resource identifiers to AWS APIs can cause unauthorized lookups, confusing errors, or unexpected resource access.
fix_summary: Validate IDs and selectors before sending them to boto3 clients.

description: Full event or request body serialised directly to console.log — PII/sensitive data exposure
impact: Customer payloads can be permanently stored in CloudWatch Logs and copied into SIEM or analytics pipelines.
fix_summary: Redact sensitive event keys before calling console logging.

description: Possible hardcoded secret — sensitive variable assigned a string literal
impact: Static secrets in source or bundles can be extracted from repositories, build logs, or Lambda artifacts.
fix_summary: Fetch secrets at runtime from Secrets Manager or SSM.

description: eval() called — code injection risk
impact: eval executes attacker-controlled JavaScript in the same process as your AWS credentials.
fix_summary: Replace eval with structured parsing or explicit command routing.

description: HTTP request made with URL from event/environment without scheme validation
impact: Attacker-supplied URLs can be used to probe internal services or metadata endpoints.
fix_summary: Construct a URL object and require https before making requests.

description: TLS verification disabled: rejectUnauthorized: false
impact: Trusting any certificate enables MITM interception and upstream spoofing.
fix_summary: Remove rejectUnauthorized:false and trust only approved certificate chains.

description: Command injection risk: child_process.exec/execSync with shell interpolation
impact: Shell interpolation lets attackers execute arbitrary commands inside the Lambda runtime.
fix_summary: Use execFile or spawn with validated argument arrays.

description: Possible SQL injection — template literal or string concatenation used to build SQL
impact: Attackers can alter SQL semantics, bypass filters, or dump sensitive rows.
fix_summary: Use placeholders and bound parameters instead of string concatenation or template literals.

description: User-controlled event field interpolated directly into log string
impact: User-supplied newline characters can forge log entries or confuse downstream analysis.
fix_summary: Normalize or escape untrusted values before interpolating them into log messages.

description: Empty catch block — errors are silently discarded
impact: Discarded exceptions hide abuse, retries, and partial processing failures.
fix_summary: Log or rethrow caught errors instead of leaving catch blocks empty.

description: Sensitive field name in returned object — may expose secrets to caller
impact: Secrets can be returned to callers or logged by downstream systems.
fix_summary: Remove sensitive fields from return values before responding.

description: Full request/event struct logged with %v or %+v — PII/sensitive data exposure
impact: Printing full request structs can expose tokens, contact details, and request bodies in logs.
fix_summary: Log only specific safe fields or implement a redacted formatter.

description: Possible hardcoded secret — sensitive variable assigned a string literal
impact: Compiled Go binaries with embedded secrets are difficult to rotate and easy to reverse-engineer.
fix_summary: Read secrets from Secrets Manager or encrypted configuration during init.

description: TLS verification disabled: InsecureSkipVerify: true
impact: Skipping certificate verification makes HTTPS susceptible to interception and impersonation.
fix_summary: Trust specific root CAs instead of setting InsecureSkipVerify.

description: Command injection risk: exec.Command with user-controlled string
impact: Passing user-controlled values into exec.Command can execute unexpected binaries or arguments.
fix_summary: Avoid shelling out, or strictly validate each argument before exec.Command.

description: Weak cryptographic algorithm: crypto/md5 or crypto/sha1 used
impact: Weak digests are collision-prone and unsuitable for security-sensitive identifiers or signatures.
fix_summary: Use sha256/sha512 or bcrypt for credentials.

description: Possible SQL injection — fmt.Sprintf used to build SQL query string
impact: String-formatted SQL allows attackers to manipulate query structure and exfiltrate data.
fix_summary: Use placeholders in QueryContext or ExecContext and bind values separately.

description: Error silently discarded with blank identifier: _ = err
impact: Ignoring errors hides failed writes, cleanup issues, and security control failures.
fix_summary: Check errors explicitly and log or return them.

description: User-controlled value passed to log.Printf — potential log injection
impact: Malicious log content can create forged records or break analytics pipelines.
fix_summary: Quote and sanitize user-derived values before sending them to log.Printf.

description: Full request/event object logged with toString() or directly — PII/sensitive data exposure
impact: Logging entire request objects or toString() output can expose tokens and personal data.
fix_summary: Log only approved fields or implement a redacted toString().

description: Possible hardcoded secret — sensitive field assigned a string literal
impact: Embedded credentials in jars are persistent and difficult to rotate across Lambda aliases and environments.
fix_summary: Inject secrets from Secrets Manager or encrypted configuration at runtime.

description: Command injection risk: Runtime.exec() or ProcessBuilder with user input
impact: Runtime.exec and ProcessBuilder can execute arbitrary commands when arguments come from the request.
fix_summary: Avoid shell commands or pass only fixed binaries plus validated arguments.

description: TLS verification disabled: TrustAllCerts or NoopHostnameVerifier in use
impact: Trust-all TLS configuration removes endpoint authentication and enables MITM attacks.
fix_summary: Use a proper TrustStore and hostname verification instead of trust-all helpers.

description: Weak cryptographic algorithm: MD5 or SHA-1 MessageDigest in use
impact: MD5 and SHA-1 are deprecated for security-sensitive hashing and signature workflows.
fix_summary: Switch to SHA-256+ and BCrypt for passwords.

description: XXE risk: DocumentBuilderFactory or SAXParserFactory without XXE protection features disabled
impact: Unsafe XML parsers can read files or trigger network requests via crafted entities.
fix_summary: Disable DTDs and external entities before parsing XML.

description: Possible SQL injection — string concatenation used to build SQL query
impact: String-built queries let attackers change WHERE clauses or execute unintended statements.
fix_summary: Use PreparedStatement placeholders and bind values.

description: Empty catch block — exception silently swallowed
impact: Empty catch blocks hide failures and make abuse or partial execution invisible.
fix_summary: Log or rethrow the exception instead of swallowing it.

description: User-controlled value concatenated directly into log statement
impact: Direct concatenation of request data can forge or split log records.
fix_summary: Use parameterized logging and sanitize user strings first.
